title: RN TradeLab v0.25 – a Scanner, a Probability Lab, and a smarter Optimizer (free desktop backtesting app)
author: RNAlgotrading

comments.author: muffledjimmie04
comments.body: The probability lab is the feature that catches my attention more than another optimizer. It's easy to find settings that look profitable historically, but understanding the range of possible outcomes is much harder. I'd love to see how it handles unseen data and poor execution assumptions. I occasionally use Moon to express price direction opinions and tools that make uncertainty visible are much more interesting than perfect looking equity curves.

replies.author: RNAlgotrading
replies.body:
Thanks, this is exactly why I built it. An optimizer can always find a setting that looked great; the harder and more useful question is "what's the realistic spread of outcomes from here?"

On your two points:

\*\*Unseen data:\*\* Probability Lab treats "now" as the last bar of whatever date range you pick. So you can set the end date back a few months, read what it says, then move the date forward and see what actually happened. That's a manual out-of-sample check on its own numbers. Every % comes with its sample size and a 95% range, and Candlestick Edge corrects for testing many patterns at once, so a few lucky ones don't look like an edge. Fair warning: the most common verdict is "not distinguishable from chance". On RELIANCE 15-min, none of the 7 classic candle patterns beat the stock's normal behaviour.

\*\*Execution:\*\* Target vs Stop is deliberately pessimistic. If one bar touches both the target and the stop, it counts as stopped, since you can't know the order inside a bar. It also shows a break-even win rate for your reward:risk. Its EV is before costs, so you'd still subtract your own slippage. For full strategies, the backtester adds slippage and commission, fills gapped-through stops at the open (worse), and the Performance Report has Monte Carlo resampling and walk-forward. So you see a fan of possible equity curves instead of one pretty line.

What it won't do is tell you direction. It tells you how often something like today has worked before, and how unsure that number is. If you try it, I'd love to hear where the uncertainty display could be clearer.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: I'd push on market twins first. nearest-neighbour lookalikes match on shape and skip the regime, so a twin from 2017 at half of today's vol gets counted next to one from last month. a twin count and a vol filter beside the odds would make me trust the panel more than the odds themselves.

replies.author: RNAlgotrading
replies.body:
That's a fair hit, and you're right. Twins are z-normalised on log price, so they match purely on shape. Volatility gets scaled away, and a calm 2017 twin sits right next to a stressed one from last month. The returns after each twin are also raw %, so a low-vol twin quietly drags the fan narrower than today's market would justify.

What's there now: the number of twins used (and how many candidates were searched), the date of each of the top matches so you can see when they come from, a 95% range on the odds, and a verdict against the stock's normal rate. What isn't there yet is the regime part, and I agree it matters more than the headline %.

What I'm planning to add:

\- A volatility filter, so only twins whose volatility was close to today's are counted (Target vs Stop already does this with volatility quintiles, so it's the same idea)

\- Each twin's volatility and date shown next to the odds, plus how many twins survived the filter

\- An option to rescale each twin's path by today's vol / its vol, so the fan is in today's units

\- Maybe a recency weight or a "last N years only" switch

Then you can compare "all twins" vs "same-regime twins". If the odds only hold in one of them, that's the answer. Thanks, this is exactly the kind of feedback I was hoping for.

replies.author: QuanTradin
replies.body: the rescale option is the one I'd ship first, it makes the fan readable in today's units without throwing twins away. the volatility filter will shrink the sample fast on a quiet stock, so the survivor count next to the odds matters more than the odds. how many twins is your floor before you refuse to print a number?
